evidence: mt3-infer is MIT licensed and wraps MR-MT3 behind a reproducible inference API.
mt3-infer documents an MR-MT3 checkpoint around 176 MB and SHA-256 verification on download.
The path is zero-optimizer and directly tests whether a different pretrained transcription prior improves Basic Pitch's precision failure.
alternatives.expectedCost: low-to-moderate: one checkpoint plus inference on the same eight short direct-input examples
alternatives.licensingRisk: low relative to the synthetic alternative, subject to pinning exact wrapper/backend/checkpoint identities before execution
alternatives.precisionRationale: MR-MT3 is sequence/multitrack transcription rather than Basic Pitch's frame/onset decoder; a predeclared guitar-program and playable-range projection can suppress obviously irrelevant instrument notes without tuning thresholds.
alternatives.mainRisk: domain mismatch remains; another generic pretrained front end may still fail on guitar-specific articulation.

evidence: SynthTab directly targets low-resource guitar tablature transcription and reports synthetic data as a way to reduce overfitting.
The released SynthTab corpus is close to 2 TB and CC BY-NC 4.0.
The repository documents known rendering bugs affecting a small percentage of total audio duration despite many tracks being touched.
A clean-room commercial-safe synthetic renderer would require additional source-instrument licensing and substantially more engineering before a scientifically useful pilot.
alternatives.expectedCost: high: dataset acquisition/rendering, storage, preprocessing, and optimizer work
alternatives.licensingRisk: high for using the released CC BY-NC dataset in a commercial product path; custom rendering reduces this but introduces sample-library provenance work
alternatives.precisionRationale: domain-specific synthetic negatives could eventually target false positives and broaden content coverage better than eight crops
alternatives.mainRisk: large engineering and licensing commitment before knowing whether a simpler pretrained front end is sufficient.

reason: It is the cheapest materially different test that directly addresses the immediate precision question without optimizer work, avoids the non-commercial SynthTab dataset constraint, and preserves the option to pursue custom synthetic pretraining later if all frozen pretrained front ends fail.
